title: Day 28: Exporting Images in Photoshop – Layered PSD, JPEG Deliverables, and Camera Raw Tweaks
summary: PHLEARN’s Day 28 walks through practical, non-destructive export workflows in Photoshop. The instructor starts with background editing by replacing city scenery with a nature backdrop using Generative Fill, then removes a logo from the subject’s hat, and groups layers. A smart-filter workflow is shown by combining layers with Apply Image and applying a Camera Raw filter to add a vignette and perform color grading (shadows, midtones, highlights) while maintaining editability. The video emphasizes saving two deliverables: a layered PSD for future edits and a flattened JPEG suitable for print, web, or social sharing. It covers export settings in depth—format choices (PSD vs JPEG vs TIFF/PDF), color space (sRGB with embedded profile), metadata handling, and scale options (1x and 0.5x) to produce multiple sizes from a single project. The result is a clear, repeatable approach to producing web- and print-ready assets from a single Photoshop document.

sections.title: Intro and export plan
sections.description: The host introduces the goal of exporting images for sharing and emphasizes saving in two formats: a layered PSD for future edits and a flattened JPEG for print/web/social use.

sections.title: Background replacement with Generative Fill
sections.description: The subject’s background is selected and replaced using Generative Fill (Nature planes), aiming to create a natural hiking scene by removing city elements in the backdrop.

sections.title: Generating background variations
sections.description: Multiple generated variations are previewed, selecting a result that places the subject in a more adventurous, natural setting.

sections.title: Hat logo removal
sections.description: The logo on the hat is removed with a painting/erase approach, demonstrating targeted object removal on a separate layer.

sections.title: Layered editing setup and Apply Image workflow
sections.description: A new layer is created and Apply Image is used to composite the edits onto that layer, preparing the file for non-destructive edits via smart filters.

sections.title: Camera Raw adjustments and smart filters
sections.description: The image is converted to a Smart Object to enable non-destructive Camera Raw edits, including a radial vignette and targeted color grading (shadows, midtones, highlights).

sections.title: Saving: PSD vs. other formats
concepts: PSD vs Large Document vs TIFF
sections.description: The workflow covers saving a layered PSD (exported file with all layers intact) and explains when to use Large Document or TIFF options for different pipelines.

sections.title: Export As workflow and deliverables
concepts: Color space: sRGB and embedded profile
sections.description: Export As settings are walked through in detail, with guidance on choosing JPEG as the default for sharing, adjusting quality, embedding sRGB color profiles, and producing multiple sizes (including a half-size variant) from a single document. The session ends with folder organization and reminders to preserve both layered and flattened outputs.
